entrypoints.summary: For each listed composite, the program reads two client-controlled lines using input(), strips them, and parses each with ast.literal_eval.
The Docker runtime exposes a socat TCP listener on port 1337 that executes main.py for connections.

affected_components.role: Parses supplied literals, applies the factor predicate, and gates success on all loop iterations.

causal_paths.kind: client input to factor acceptance comparison

code_slices.fixed: No supplied patch. A derived repair is to reject values unless both operands are intended integer values (excluding bool where appropriate) before multiplication.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The loop iterates over seven composites, continues on acceptance, and prints flag.txt only through the loop else branch.
code_slices.vulnerable: Each input is parsed with ast.literal_eval; check_factors performs abs checks, rejects only type(a*b) == float, and returns a*b == ab.

negative_controls: Any failed check breaks the loop before the success branch.
A product whose exact type is float is rejected with "no floats please".
An operand with absolute value at most one is rejected with "too easy".
observability.positive_marker: The source specifies "Here is your Flag. Good Job!" followed by the contents of flag.txt after all iterations pass.

preconditions: The attacker can reach the TCP service exposed by the supplied Docker configuration.
The attacker supplies syntax accepted by ast.literal_eval.
A full success requires satisfying each of the seven loop iterations; no supplied artifact proves a complete construction.

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of the factor-verification gate and the gated success/flag-output path.
impact.attacker_capability: A remote client can submit literal-evaluable non-integer values that are not excluded by the float-product-only filter and can attempt to advance a verification iteration when their multiplication compares equal to that iteration's target.
impact.security_effect: The verifier can accept an operand domain broader than intended, weakening integrity of an individual factor-verification decision; a full challenge-success result would additionally require accepted inputs for every listed composite.

causal_trace.summary: A client supplies purported factor values as Python literal text; each value is parsed by ast.literal_eval before verification.
The verifier does not establish that either parsed operand is an integer factor. It rejects operands with absolute value at most one and rejects only products whose exact type is float.

The acceptance decision directly evaluates language-level multiplication and equality, returning a*b == ab after the narrow float-product check; admitted non-float literal values therefore reach this comparison.
Each accepted comparison advances the loop. Only after every listed composite is accepted does the program print a success message and read and print flag.txt.

primary_invariant.statement: A successful factor check must require two intended integer-domain factors, each outside the trivial absolute-value range, whose product equals the requested composite.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Operands are accepted from ast.literal_eval without an integer-type check; the implementation filters only a float-valued product before evaluating multiplication and equality.

quality.review_notes: The primary source code and container configuration establish the input path, narrow float filter, comparison operation, TCP exposure, and success branch. No solver, interaction transcript, or test run establishes a concrete non-integer construction accepted for all seven targets. The bundled flag is a fake fixture, and no remediation patch is provided; remediation is a code-derived invariant-restoration recommendation.

remediation.invariant_restored: Before multiplication, require both parsed operands to be integer values in the intended domain (and exclude bool if it is not intended); then apply the nontriviality and product-equality checks.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A TCP client connects to the deployed listener and provides two literal text lines for each iteration reached.
